text: Module twelve. Otesha Connect — the API a partner builds against.

None of it existed until somebody granted it. A partner is not a second organisation: it is a corporate account with API access, so granting creates the partner identity, issues sandbox credentials and links them in one call.
And withdrawing keeps the settlement history. It suspends the partner and unlinks it — a statement about who may call the API, not a reason to lose what they were owed.
On the client's side, a console with six steps in the order they have to happen. Create a sandbox key, get a token, link a test customer, place an order, listen for webhooks, go live.
The key's secret is shown once, when the key is created. Lose it and you make another — that is the intended path, not a failure of it.
The sandbox is a world you can break. Reset wipes it and re-seeds two hundred trees across all ten lifecycle states, five caretakers, five customers, and a year of back-dated visits.
And you can move a tree's clock — ninety days, a year — to exercise milestones in an afternoon. The tree's clock, not the server's: a shared clock would mean your test changed somebody else's data.
Webhooks are HTTPS only, because over plain HTTP the payload and its signature are both readable by anything on the path, which makes the signature pointless.
Three of the events are marked no producer yet. They are declared so an integration can be written against them, and marked so nobody waits on a call that never comes.
Usage separates two questions people conflate. New accounts are the ones your integration opened; customers linked includes people who already had Otesha before they met your app.

And a settlement statement is compiled from the same basis as that usage report, so the two agree. Once issued it is never edited — a correction is issued beside it, because somebody has already filed the original.
Writing this module found something worse than a missing page. Six pages were still saying Placeholder — this page is a stub for the structural trial — on the live site.
All eight checks had passed the whole time. They ask whether links resolve and whether figures rebuild. A stub has neither, so it sails through every one of them.
Two are now written, one was deleted for restating another page, one became this module's credentials page, and two are genuinely blocked — so they say so, in the words of the thing blocking them.
Eight pages, and a ninth check that would have caught the other six.
